title: System prompt debug route is exposed without route-level authorization
reasoning: The GET /api/sdk/system-prompt handler accepts network query parameters, including user_id/model selection, builds the effective debug config, and returns the raw system_prompt. The route signature has no visible authentication, authorization, or debug-mode guard dependency, so any caller able to reach this SDK router could retrieve internal prompt instructions and potentially request another user's effective prompt by supplying user_id. If this router is mounted only behind a global auth/debug gate elsewhere, that would mitigate the issue, but no such protection is present in the included owned file.
recommendation: Require an explicit authorization/debug capability check for this route before building or returning the prompt. Bind user_id to the authenticated principal or remove arbitrary user_id selection unless the caller has an admin/debug permission. Consider returning redacted prompt metadata by default and raw prompt text only under a deliberate debug flag.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the excerpt does not show any route-level test asserting unauthorized callers are rejected or that user_id is constrained to the caller.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add FastAPI route tests for GET /api/sdk/system-prompt covering unauthenticated rejection, non-admin cross-user user_id rejection, and authorized debug/admin access returning the expected response shape.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/routes/sdk/router.py route dependency or shared SDK debug-route guard used by this handler
